title: Acute appendicitis in a patient immunised with COVID-19 vaccine: A case report with morphological analysis.
ehr_evidence: The study is a single-patient case report; data were derived from clinical assessment, imaging (abdominal ultrasound and contrast CT), laboratory tests, and histopathological analysis of one 58-year-old female at Careggi University Hospital, not from an electronic/computerised health record.
summary: A case report of a 58-year-old female who developed acute appendicitis approximately 48 hours after her first Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine dose, with morphological analysis revealing granulomatous inflammation.
key_findings: A 58-year-old female developed acute appendicitis approximately 48 hours after her first Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine dose; histology showed diffuse acute and chronic inflammatory infiltrates with scattered non-necrotizing granulomas throughout the appendiceal wall.
WHO causality assessment (2018 algorithm) yielded B1: temporal relationship consistent but insufficient definitive evidence that the vaccine caused the event.
captured_features: Clinical presentation (right iliac fossa pain, fever, nausea, vomiting)
Ultrasound findings (fluid collection in right iliac fossa, cecal wall thickening)
CT scan findings (distended appendix, maximum thickness 12 mm, thickened walls)
Laboratory values (haemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, leukocytosis 12.1x10^9/L, neutrophilia 78.4%, fibrinogen 636.0 mg/dL, prothrombin time 13.3 s)
Histopathology (acute and chronic infiltrates, non-necrotizing granulomas within lymphoid follicles, serosal giant cells)
data_source_type: Other (single-patient clinical case report with morphological analysis)
population: A single 58-year-old female academic healthcare professional at Careggi University Hospital, Florence, Italy (adult patient, not pediatric)
limitations: Single-patient case report; cannot establish causation or association.
No causal relationship between COVID-19 vaccine and appendicitis established.
data_availability_statement: Data are available upon reasonable request to the corresponding author.
